source.title: Entropic gradient descent algorithms and wide flat minima
source.authors: Fabrizio Pittorino; Carlo Lucibello; Christoph Feinauer; E. M. Malatesta; Gabriele Perugini; Carlo Baldassi; Matteo Negri; E. Demyanenko; R. Zecchina

record.tranche_reason: Measures local energy and test error together using the same multiplicative weight perturbation measure, on additional network settings.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports test-error comparisons for SGD, eSGD and rSGD, but those results alone do not measure the flatness–generalization relation in V7. Values visible only in figures are recorded as figure only; the text does not give precise curve values.
record.test_reason: The study measures magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sensitivity alongside generalization in additional network settings (V7), and directly compares dropout with no dropout in a fully connected classifier (V6). It is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report agreement between local entropy and local energy, associations with generalization, and generally better generalization from entropic algorithms. They qualify the flatness comparison by requiring similar training errors and comparisons within the same architecture.
record.recipe_differences: The local-energy measure uses multiplicative weight perturbations, as in the cited generalization-measure work; this paper applies it in shallow and deep network experiments and also measures local entropy in the shallow setting.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that flatness and test-error correlation is not observed when compared minima have different training errors. Local entropy and local energy are only comparable within the same architecture. In the shallow committee machine, dropout probability changes the measured flatness and test-error distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: Entropic optimizers generally improve held-out performance relative to their baselines in Table 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing local entropy can improve image-classifier test performance under the tested training budgets.

record.problems: Some comparisons are figure-only without tabulated values. The authors qualify the flatness–generalization relation: it is sensitive to training-error matching, and the local-energy comparison is restricted to a fixed architecture. The PGDL correlation is observational.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 test-error comparisons between SGD and entropic algorithms were left out because they do not measure the local-energy–generalization relation in V7. Additional architecture-specific flatness curves in Figures 4 and 5 were not extracted separately; the paper describes their agreement with generalization as generally good, without tabulating curve values.

untested.parts: Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Convolutional dropout comparisons, training-set-size dependence, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.

Ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; SVHN; the specified convolutional setting without augmentation; and verification of matched training fit and generalization gaps in the PGDL comparison.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The dropout experiment need not test every clause of V6 to support its tested regime. Missing direct gap information in R4 is an evidential limitation, not a demonstrated failure of V7. The stated failure with unequal training errors lies outside V7's matched-fit condition. Figures 4 and 5 are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison of the kind described.
Dropout is varied in a shallow-network appendix, but the paper does not test the full version’s stated dropout regimes or removal of dropout and weight decay together.

The paper measures local energy using multiplicative weight noise and relates it to test error, but does not test the specified CIFAR-10 and SVHN convolutional-family setting without data augmentation, nor compare against the stated norm- and margin-based measures. The relation is correlational.

rows.measure: Ranking of local energy profiles and test errors across algorithms
rows.value: Text states the ranking of the two flatness measures is preserved and flatter minima generalize better; exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: 50 random restarts; no error bar or significance test stated for this comparison.
rows.note: The text describes the cross-algorithm ranking; curve and distribution values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: This extends the flatness–generalization comparison to a shallow committee machine. Appendix B.1 specifies zero-training-error solutions, so test error also measures the generalization gap. The cross-algorithm ranking is explicitly described in prose; evidence is not exclusively figure-only.

rows.subject: committee machine
rows.size_stated: Input size N = 784; single hidden layer with K = 9 hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Measured local energy profiles and test-error distributions for SGD fast with different dropout probabilities.
rows.measure: Local energy and test error across dropout conditions
rows.value: Text states that minima obtained with higher dropout have larger local entropy and generalize better; exact local-energy curves and test-error distributions are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: 50 random restarts; no error bar or significance test stated for this comparison.
rows.note: The prose specifically mentions local entropy and test error; the plotted local-energy profiles are not numerically described in the text.
rows.check: Also directly tests V6: dropout probabilities 0.25 and 0.4 improve generalization relative to no dropout. Appendix B.3 explicitly states that local energy and local entropy both correlate with generalization in this setting, so the reader's proposed V7 limitation is unsupported.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared local-energy curves and test errors at matched training stages for SGD, eSGD and rSGD.
rows.measure: Local energy profile versus test error
rows.value: Text states eSGD and rSGD curves are below the SGD curve across a wide range of σ values while achieving better generalization; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The figure reports selected epoch, unperturbed train and test errors in its legends; curves are not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: Figure 3 provides readable final train/test errors (%): SGD 0.15/13.3, eSGD 0.12/11.8, rSGD 0.02/11.9. Corresponding gaps are 13.15, 11.68 and 11.88 percentage points. Final cross-entropy losses are 0.005, 0.01 and 0.005. Perturbation-curve values remain untabulated; these experiments use data augmentation.

dropout, batch size and weight decay

rows.measure: Pearson correlation between local energy (train error difference at σ = 0.5) and test error
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation over 64 perturbation realizations for each point; p-value 1e-4
rows.note: The reported correlation is across models with different generalization errors; the paper says local entropy and local energy are comparable only within the same architecture.
rows.check: The reported r(12) = 0.90, p = 1e-4 establishes correlation with test error. Unperturbed training errors/losses for these PGDL models are not supplied, so this row alone cannot establish correlation with the generalization gap among similarly fitted models.
